subject: BrightLayer discovery — capacity profile and target unit economics
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: BrightLayer discovery — follow-up & ask: per-model volumes and target $/1M tokens

Hi Amit — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so your procurement and engineering teams can align: 

Summary of the call:
- BrightLayer will embed LLM features into search and summarization flows for clinical docs and internal KBs.
- Primary user-facing functions: chat assistant (clinical triage), embeddings for semantic search, and a small reranking step for search results.
- Initial pilot: 3-month POC, then roll to production if latency and unit costs meet target.

Asks / open questions (would you confirm the items below?):
1) Expected monthly token volumes by model type during pilot and steady-state (estimates are fine):
   - chat prompts + completions (tokens/month) — pilot / steady-state
   - embeddings calls (num vectors/month + average tokens/input)
   - rerank calls (requests/month + avg tokens/context)
2) Target unit economics: you mentioned a target around $X per 1M tokens — can you confirm a target range (e.g., $250–$600 per 1M tokens) or an absolute $/1M token?
3) Latency & SLA expectations for chat (p50/p95) and availability requirements for dedicated capacity vs hosted API.
4) Any compliance constraints (data residency, SOC2 evidence, KMS requirements) we should pre-load into the procurement packet.

Attached: placeholder for the usage CSV you offered to share (BrightLayer_USAGE_Q3.csv). We’ll queue up an initial cost projection once we have the volume breakdown — I included Marissa (pricing) and Logan (solutions) to help with an initial costed scenario and a draft SOW.

Proposed next steps:
- Amit to share the pilot/steady-state volume estimates and any usage samples (BrightLayer_USAGE_Q3.csv).
- Redwood to return a 3-scenario cost sketch (conservative / expected / optimistic) with model-mix assumptions and expected $/1M token implications.
- If volumes & target $/1M align, we’ll propose an initial Dedicated capacity quote and a canary rollout plan.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short pricing note tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin

Subject: Re: BrightLayer discovery — follow-up & ask: per-model volumes and target $/1M tokens

Thanks Soojin — useful recap. See answers inline and attached preliminary usage export (BrightLayer_USAGE_Q3.csv).

Quick answers:
- Pilot (month 1–3):
  - chat: ~120M tokens/month (prompt+completion), primarily short assistant exchanges (average 120 tokens per convo).
  - embeddings: 90k calls/month, average 256 tokens per input (we embed paragraphs).
  - rerank: 45k requests/month, average 600 tokens of context (we do 5 candidate reranks).
- Steady-state (post-rollout 6+ months):
  - chat: 420M tokens/month
  - embeddings: 420k calls/month
  - rerank: 180k requests/month
- Target unit economics: Procurement prefers cost ~ $350 per 1M tokens equivalent as a blended target for budgeting. If we can get below $300 we’ll be very competitive.
- Latency: p95 chat target <= 450ms; p50 < 100ms would be great. Availability: 99.9% SLA preferred for production.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required; data residency in US only for now; KMS integration required.

We attached the usage extract. Let us know if you need additional fields (session ids, nonce).

Amit

Subject: RE: BrightLayer discovery — follow-up & ask: per-model volumes and target $/1M tokens

Amit / team — thanks for the breakdown, this is excellent. I ran a quick back-of-envelope against three model mix scenarios and included a short summary below. I’ve attached a simple Excel with assumptions (Redwood_Instance_Specs.xlsx).

Key assumptions I used:
- Model choices: chat => gpt-4o-like dense chat variant; embeddings => small-dim instruction-tuned embedding; rerank => compact encoder with rerank head.
- Pricing proxy: we size compute per inference and then convert to $/1M tokens using projected throughput and batching gains.

3 scenario sketches (monthly cost, blended $/1M tokens):
1) Conservative (safe configs, minimal quantization): $18k/mo pilot => blended $/1M = $450
2) Expected (some quantization + batching, autoscaling): $11.5k/mo pilot => blended $/1M = $290
3) Optimistic (strong batching, prefix caching, Dedicated reserved): $8.2k/mo pilot => blended $/1M = $205

Model mix inputs used for pilot sketch (please confirm):
- Chat: 65% of token volume
- Embeddings: 25% of calls but small proportion of token volume (roughly 20% of cost)
- Rerank: 10% of calls but high per-call token context (roughly 15% of cost)

Questions for Amit:
- Can you confirm whether embeddings will accept per-call batching (i.e., sending N texts per request) or if you’ll call 1 per request? That materially affects cost.
- For rerank, do you expect to rank 5 candidates every request consistently?

Next steps: 
- If $/1M target of $350 is the procurement guardrail, both our Expected and Optimistic scenarios look promising; we’ll prepare a formal pilot quote that maps to the DL-2026-078-BL deal.
- Logan, can you prepare a latency/canary plan for the pilot (region selection + fallback to hosted variants) and a config for prefix/KV caching?

Thanks — will pull a one-page pricing summary for Amit tomorrow.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

- Rerank: yes, 5 candidates consistently.
- Procurement notes: can you include an option for a 12-month reserved Dedicated band with an overage rate? If the reserved commitment hits steady-state we can then convert to long-term.

Please send a concise pilot quote (1–2 pages) with the three scenarios and an explicit line showing blended $/1M tokens and an option for a 12-month reserved discount. I’ve looped in ProcureOps for scheduling a procurement sync on Tues 8/18.
